title: the cairn device's metrics verb answers totals
intention: The cairn device's metrics verb answers totals (outline 17.27.2: 'so any metric can be reported fast'): cairn/devices/cairn/metrics.py gains totals(table, *, name, source, since, until, by, roots), which collects then answers one {name, count, sum} per metric name (and per info[by] when by is given) summed in the table; report gains until; the verb routes a body with totals true to totals.
why: Measured 2026-11-10: the metrics verb answers only raw rows; inference_calls holds 22,156 calls, which metered per call are ~66k rows at ~440 bytes, so every yield report over the verb would carry ~23 MB.
how: A totals function and an until keyword in the module; the verb routes on totals; a red-first proof over scratch tables.

clauses.claim: totals answers one total per metric name: count is every matching row, a row with no value included; sum adds the values, a valueless row adding nothing
totals with by='verdict' answers one total per name and info.verdict
since and until bound the totals (both inclusive), and report honors until
the cairn device's metrics verb, with totals true in its body, answers json-serialisable totals grouped by the body's by, and no rows

decisions.text: D1: cairn/devices/cairn/metrics.py, copied whole from the chart's module: a helper _where(name, source, since, until) builds the 'name = %s', 'source = %s', 'at >= %s', 'at <= %s' fragments and their params; report gains a keyword until and uses _where; totals(table=TABLE, *, name=None, source=None, since=None, until=None, by=None, roots=None) collects, then store.query('SELECT name[, info ->> %s AS "by"], count(*) AS count, coalesce(sum(value), 0) AS sum FROM {t} [WHERE ...] GROUP BY 1[, 2] ORDER BY 1[, 2]', tables={'t': table}, params=([by] +) where params), returning {'collected': n, 'totals': [{name, [by,] count as int, sum as float}]}. It deletes nothing.

D2: cairn/devices/cairn/device.py: _handle_metrics passes name, source, since, until and roots; when body.get('totals') is truthy it returns metrics.totals(table, by=body.get('by'), **kw), otherwise metrics.report(table, **kw). Nothing else changes.

D3: the charter cairn/devices/cairn/intention+why.json, through the artifact door (cairn artifact write --verb cast --from a scratch copy): its 'what' gains, appended after one space, exactly this sentence: "Asked with totals true, the metrics verb answers one count and sum per metric name, optionally split by an info key, so a report over all time stays small." Every other field stands as it is.

D4: the proof cairn/devices/cairn/proofs/test_the_metrics_verb_answers_totals.py, red-first, one tooth per clause, PROVES f4dbcea5a117 1-4. Its world is a temp roots dict with one holder, instance/devices/inference_domain/0, recording three calls (a miss spending 10 at 2026-01-01, a hit saving 4 at 2026-02-01, a miss spending 6 at 2026-03-01), each a spent, a saved and a valueless latency row with info.verdict, through cairn.tools.metric against a temp charter. Each tooth uses store.scratch('cairn', 'mtot', metric.COLUMNS). The live 'metrics' table is never touched.

measured.saw: 22,156 rows in inference_calls; 63 metrics records waiting, ~440 bytes each; the verb answers rows only
measured.how: store.query count(*) on inference_calls; wc on the inference_domain metrics recorder; grep -n report cairn/devices/cairn/device.py
